_note: The INBOUND half of WebMCP (proposals/webmcp.md §4): the PAGE TOOL TABLE a shell keeps when a web surface's page registers tools through `document.modelContext`. This is the registration API local-ai-engine.md §4.6 named as a launch tool source and never specified; the standard is now that spelling, so the table below is what a Despia shell must agree on before any WebKit or android.webkit line is written. THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) THE TABLE IS POLICY-FREE. It records, validates and forgets; approval, ordering and dispatch belong to the consumer (the agent loop), exactly as the bridge relays and never decides. (2) VALIDATION IS THE SPEC'S — name 1..128 of ASCII alphanumeric plus `_ - .`, a non-empty description — and a rejected registration records NOTHING and emits no change event, because the spec rejects the promise and a half-registered tool is worse than none. (3) A DUPLICATE NAME IS REFUSED AND THE INCUMBENT SURVIVES; the spec rejects the second registerTool, so last-write-wins would silently swap a tool under an agent mid-session. (4) SCHEMAS PASS THROUGH VERBATIM — `oneOf`, `pattern`, `format`, nesting, all of it. Down-converting a foreign schema to our vocabulary would silently narrow what the model can express (the ai/tools law, same sentence). (5) A PAGE'S TOOLS DIE WITH THE PAGE: a navigation commit on a surface drops every row the previous document registered, including a same-origin reload, because it is a NEW document with a new callback registry. (6) EVERY REGISTRATION CARRIES PROVENANCE — the registering origin and the surface — so a consumer can tell a tool from the app's own origin from one an embedded page offered, and so a description stays attributable. (7) A DESCRIPTION IS UNTRUSTED INPUT and an ANNOTATION IS A HINT: `readOnlyHint` is recorded, and it NEVER lowers the approval a page-sourced tool needs. A page cannot vouch for itself, so the trust decision is the consumer's and its default is `required`. (8) THE ABORT SIGNAL IS THE UNREGISTER PATH — one row leaves, the rest stay. (9) A CHANGE THAT ALTERS THE VISIBLE SET EMITS EXACTLY ONE `toolchange` FOR ITS SURFACE, so a consumer re-reads once rather than diffing. (10) SURFACES ARE ISOLATED: two surfaces may each carry a `search`, and dropping one leaves the other whole.

cases.name: registry: a valid registration is recorded with its provenance
cases._note: The canonical inbound case. The page wrote the schema, so the schema is the contract and the table keeps it byte for byte.

tool.name: track-order
tool.description: Look up the status of an order by number.

tools.name: track-order
tools.description: Look up the status of an order by number.

cases.name: registry: an arbitrary JSON Schema survives verbatim
cases._note: oneOf, a pattern, a nested object and additionalProperties:false all reach the model unchanged. A table that normalised this would narrow what the page can express and no test would ever see the loss.

tool.name: cart.addItem
tool.description: Add an item to the cart.

tools.name: cart.addItem
tools.description: Add an item to the cart.

cases.name: registry: readOnlyHint is recorded and does not lower approval
cases._note: A page vouching for itself is not evidence. The hint is kept because a consumer may weigh it, and the approval it would have bought is withheld because the page is the party asking.

cases.name: registry: an invalid name is refused typed and records nothing
cases._note: The spec rejects the promise; the table's twin of that is a rejection with a reason and an unchanged set. No toolchange, because nothing changed.

cases.name: registry: an empty description is refused typed
cases._note: Required by the spec, and useless to a model besides.

cases.name: registry: a duplicate name is refused and the incumbent survives
cases._note: The second registration loses. Last-write-wins would let a page swap a tool's behaviour under an agent that had already read its description.

cases.name: registry: a navigation commit drops the previous page's tools
cases._note: A page's tools die with the page. The callbacks they name live in a JavaScript heap that no longer exists, so a row that outlived its document would be a tool that always fails.

cases.name: registry: a same-origin reload drops them too
cases._note: Same origin, same URL, new document. Comparing origins to decide would keep rows whose closures were collected on reload.

cases.name: registry: a commit with nothing registered emits no change
cases._note: Navigation is constant in a web surface. An event per commit would wake every consumer on every page load for no reason, so the event tracks the SET, not the navigation.

cases.name: registry: abort removes one row and leaves the rest
cases._note: The spec's unregister path is the AbortSignal passed at registration. One tool leaves; a page that registered five keeps four.

cases.name: registry: aborting an unknown row changes nothing and says nothing
cases._note: An abort can arrive after a navigation already dropped the row. Emitting a change for a set that did not change would be a lie a consumer acts on.

cases.name: registry: surfaces are isolated
cases._note: Two bare surfaces may each host a page offering `search`. They are different pages, so they are different tools, and dropping one leaves the other whole. A consumer disambiguates by the surface it asked for.

cases.name: registry: rows read back in registration order within a surface
cases._note: The order the page registered in is the order it meant. Sorting here would fight the author for no gain a consumer asked for.
